sanskrit_verse: समूलसस्यनाशे तु तत्स्वामी समम् आप्नुयात् । वधेन पालो मुच्येत दण्डं स्वामिनि पातयेत् ॥
transliteration: samūlasasyanāśe tu tatsvāmī samam āpnuyāt | vadhena pālo mucyeta daṇḍaṃ svāmini pātayet ||
sph_interpretive_translation: When the entire crop is destroyed, the owner thereof shall incur equal loss; the protector is absolved through forfeiture of life, and the penalty falls upon the master.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from ownership and stewardship
Causation aligns with conscious capacity to prevent or allow harm
Responsibility is assigned based on ontological proximity to outcome
Restoration occurs through alignment with natural consequence, not imposed judgment
Consciousness determines true liability, not form or title
executable_legal_axioms: IF total destruction of resource occurs AND ownership is established THEN owner assumes proportional experiential completion
IF guardian/protector demonstrates causal innocence via integrity verification THEN exemption from liability is granted automatically
IF master holds positional authority over causal chain THEN liability transference to master is executed by default
NO punitive valuation is computed; all consequences are restorative in nature
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that ultimate authority bears intrinsic liability. Where a custodian or enforcer proves absence of causal misconduct through verified consciousness alignment, immunity is immediate. Liability transfers upward along the axis of authoritative control, ensuring justice as restoration rather than retribution.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that loss manifests where ownership resides, thus confirming karmic-anthropological causality. Anupūrvaśaḥ indicates sequential unfolding: negligence → failure → collapse → consequence. The forfeiture of life (vadha) here signifies dissolution of false identity, not literal death. Daṇḍa is not punitive but realigning—reintegrating misaligned consciousness back into dharmic flow without residual suffering.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Owner undergoes experiential assimilation of loss to restore energetic balance
Integrity Verification Protocol: Guardian's consciousness is scanned for causal dissonance; if none found, automatic release is enacted
Authority-Liability Mapping: Master’s role in enabling causal field is analyzed; liability reallocated accordingly
Consciousness Reintegration Sequence: All involved parties engage in guided awareness restoration to prevent recurrence
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of Sanatana Dharma: Justice originates in consciousness, operates through capacity-aware causality, and culminates in non-punitive restoration. There is no punishment. There is only awakening. Dharma is restored.
